# mac-sysdash

> A tiny, dependency-light system + GitHub Actions self-hosted runner dashboard for macOS. One Python file (stdlib + psutil) serves a JSON API and a single static HTML page; several Macs show each other's stats over Tailscale, in the browser or an optional menu bar app. No cloud, no accounts, no token, no build step for the dashboard.

mac-sysdash is source-available under the MIT License + Commons Clause: free to use for any purpose, including inside a company / for commercial operations — you just may not *sell* the software itself. It is an independent project, not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Apple, GitHub, Tailscale, Anthropic, or OpenAI.

## Key features

- Live CPU / memory / disk ring gauges and sparklines, refreshing every second, with a per-core view and a disk-fill ETA
- Self-hosted GitHub Actions runner status (busy / idle / offline) with the live job's PR, branch, commit, and actor — read from the runner's local files, never the GitHub API (no token)
- Multi-machine "fleet" view over a Tailscale tailnet (or a LAN with `SYSDASH_ALLOW=lan`); a hub pulls each peer's stats server-side, or peers push to it; offline and unreachable Macs are listed
- Optional native macOS menu bar app (macOS 14+): an overview tab plus one tab per machine, with a Settings window (Open at login, Show in Dock, icon-only mode); reads only the hub's HTTP API
- Tailnet-only access by default (loopback + Tailscale addresses); settings in `~/.config/mac-sysdash/config`
- CI health: per-runner 30-day heatmap, flaky-job detection, queue-pressure, and a Gantt timeline, backed by a local SQLite database
- Alerts: thresholds, offline-runner mutes, a snooze/maintenance mode, an optional webhook, and cron dead-man checks
- AI Copilot quota tracking: every provider enabled in CodexBar (Claude, Codex, Cursor, Antigravity, …) — session + weekly usage, read locally; the optional codexbar CLI fills gaps when the launchd agent cannot read the snapshot
- Light / dark / night themes, a wall-mounted TV mode, widget pinning, an installable offline PWA, and EN/TR

## Install

- Requirements: macOS; Homebrew *or* Python 3.9+ (one dependency: `psutil`)
- **Homebrew (recommended):**
  `brew tap berkayturanci/mac-sysdash https://github.com/berkayturanci/mac-sysdash && brew install mac-sysdash && brew services start mac-sysdash`
  (Homebrew 6+: `brew trust berkayturanci/mac-sysdash` once if refused as untrusted); menu bar app: `mac-sysdash menubar`
- Git clone + launchd: `git clone https://github.com/berkayturanci/mac-sysdash.git && cd mac-sysdash && ./install.sh`
- Or run it yourself: `python3 -m venv venv && ./venv/bin/pip install psutil && ./venv/bin/python server.py` (serves on port 8765)
- Do not run both Homebrew `brew services` and `./install.sh` — they install separate launchd agents on the same default port
